answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds bind each validator's stake to a verifiable delay function, making the marginal cost of forging a Sybil identity equal to the foregone yield on locked copper collateral. A subgame-perfect slashing matrix, enforced via zero-knowledge proofs, imposes a penalty that exceeds any possible ripple gain, rendering the expected attack utility strictly negative. Consequently the protocol converges to a strict Nash equilibrium in which no rational agent can profitably multiply identities within the grove of validators.
